articles.title: Khushbu's Youth Olympics silver gives Siddi community a new sporting hero
articles.summary: PANAJI: Now based in London, former India goalkeeper Juje Siddi has not been following all that’s happening in Indian sports, but Khushbu Darjada’s silver
articles.body: PANAJI: Now based in London, former India goalkeeper Juje Siddi has not been following all that’s happening in Indian sports, but Khushbu Darjada’s silver medal at the Youth Olympics didn’t escape his attention.Darjada took silver in the women’s judo 63kg category in Senegal, the first Olympic medal won by any member of the Siddi community.“This is good news for everyone, particularly the community,” said Juje, the first from the Siddi tribe to represent the country and win gold at the SAFF Championship in 1997. “The feat will motivate so many others from the community to take to sport and win laurels.”Ever since his move to Salgaocar SC in 1994, Juje has stood out for his distinctive look and ‘African’ features. The goalkeeper belongs to the marginalised Siddi community, descendants of East Africans who were brought to India more than five centuries ago. The Siddis have lived in relative seclusion, most on the margins of poverty.“In the 90s, we had good support (from the govt) but now that’s no longer the case. There is private coaching being conducted but coaches are not serious enough. You must prioritise the interest of the community. If the govt steps in, there’s plenty to gain. Siddis are genetically built strong, have great physique and very good in sports,” said the Karwar-born Juje.In 1987, the Sports Authority of India (SAI), spearheaded by the then Union minister of sports Margaret Alva, set up a sports scheme to scout and train members of the community. The Siddi people had athletic abilities, and Juje was among those scouted as part of the Special Area Games (SAG) scheme.He was scouted as an athlete, but when he moved to Bengaluru for schooling, his goalkeeping abilities got noticed. He did well and made it to the India U-16 camp. His selection to the India U-19 team convinced him that he was on the right track.Soon, he was spotted by coach Norbert Gonsalves during a camp in Patiala for Salgaocar.“We were lucky to be part of the SAG scheme. They suddenly stopped the project,” said the goalkeeper.The goalkeeper enjoyed a memorable career with Salgaocar, winning every major trophy in Indian football, including the National Football League in 1999.After his retirement, he took to coaching. Juje had to move to the UK in 2019. Now, at 53, he wants to return and give back to the community that shaped him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Azzi Fudd's breakup with Paige Bueckers sparks fresh questions about her WNBA future and Dallas Wings connection
articles.summary: Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers are no longer together, and they say the split happened more than a year ago.
articles.body: Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers are no longer together, and they say the split happened more than a year ago. The Dallas Wings teammates shared it on November 6 during an episode of Fudd’s podcast, “Fudd Around and Find Out.” The timing is the real news. They broke up before Dallas took Fudd first overall in April, and before they shared a locker room for the 2026 season. Bueckers also dismissed any idea that their relationship shaped the pick. Neither player shared details about why it ended, and Fudd made clear the rest stays private.Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers confirm breakup on podcastBoth laughed at the start, but Fudd kept it blunt. “We are no longer together. I don’t know how else to say that,” she said. Bueckers gave the timeline. “It’s been over a year.”Then she took on the draft chatter. “We were not together before she got drafted, so all of those narratives can go to bed,” Bueckers said. “She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it.” That second line matters because Dallas never answered the question when it first came up. At Fudd’s introductory press conference in April, a reporter asked if the two were still a couple. Wings public relations cut in before Fudd could speak.The online noise pushed them to speak. “We’ve seen a lot of negativity. We’ve seen a lot of hate,” Bueckers said, and she added that messages had reached their families and friends. Her explanation for the split was short. “Sometimes in life, there’s just seasons.”What the breakup means for Fudd and the WingsThe split did not hurt the basketball. Fudd averaged 13.1 points as a rookie, fourth among first-year players, and shot 39.7 percent from three. That shooting gives Bueckers more room to work. Bueckers made her second straight All-Star team.Dallas won a franchise-record 27 games and made the playoffs for the first time in three years. The Wings then lost in the first round to Golden State, which went on to win the title. Because the breakup came before the season, the team played every game with two former No. 1 picks who were no longer a couple. That makes this a fair test, and the results held up. It also makes them the first college teammates to go first overall in back-to-back drafts since Tina Charles in 2010 and Maya Moore in 2011.Bueckers said both will eventually move on and see other people. Until then, the work comes first. “We’re the utmost professional. We care about basketball, and we’re still friends,” she said. Fudd had a request for fans too: “we don’t need messages on what the other person is doing.”For Dallas, 2027 comes down to basketball. Can Fudd keep shooting near 40 percent in year two? How much better can two guards get with a full season of reps together?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Merritt Island Christian wins thriller, advances to state semifinals
articles.summary: In a back-and-forth game, Merritt Island Christian made the final stand in a 51-50 win over Bradenton Christian to advance to the state semifinals.
articles.body:
MERRITT ISLAND — In the playoffs, a series of individual plays could make all the difference of advancing or going home.

That was on full display on Nov. 6 for Merritt Island Christian in the SSAA 8-man state playoffs versus reigning state runner-up Bradenton Christian.

The top-seeded Cougars fell behind by double-digits early, rallied to take the lead only for Bradenton Christian to have a shot to win it on the final possession.

In a game featuring 101 total points, it was the Cougars defense that made the biggest play of the game stopping Bradenton Christian 20 yards short of a game-winning touchdown in a 51-50 win.

"I can't even begin to tell you how proud I am of this team," Merritt Island Christian head coach Josh Babin said. "Every single player, whether they're a starter or a role player, they're phenomenal. It's just been an amazing season."

In a high-scoring game, Merritt Island Christian's defense made some timely stops. The Cougars forced three turnovers on downs with two leading to touchdowns and one preserving a lead.

"It's bend, but don't break. We knew they were going to score. I think the thing that impresses me most about this team, especially (tonight), is nobody gave up," Babin said. "Nobody hung their heads. Nobody said, 'Oh we're down again and it's over.' They all fought through it. They rose above everything. They're a great team, great bunch of kids."

With the Cougars trailing 28-25 in the first half, they forced a four-and-out to get the ball back at their own 40-yard line. Just two plays later, senior Maddux Martinson rushed for a 50-yard touchdown with 4:28 left in the second quarter.

Bradenton Christian drove the ball to the Cougars 5-yard line in the final minute of the first half. Merritt Island Christian stopped the Panthers on four consecutive plays, including a tackle for loss by eighth grader Waylon Perkins on 4th-and-goal. That kept the Cougars in the lead at halftime.

"We had a long talk at halftime. There was a different look in their eye (tonight)," Babin said. "It wasn't the we're not sure what to do. Everybody knew what they needed to do and they did it. It was the most hyped I've seen this team."

In the second half, Bradenton Christian was threatening just outside the red zone leading 34-32 in the third quarter. On a 4th-and-2 at the Cougars 22-yard line, junior Mason Van Slyke wrapped up Panthers freshman Cohen Fuller for a loss of 8 yards.

Merritt Island Christian answered with a go-ahead 11-yard touchdown run by junior Korbin Kugler that put the Cougars in the lead for good.

"There's so many plays. You can dissect the whole game and if that one play doesn't happen, it could be a completely different outcome," Babin said. "I mean our kicker (Brighton Sadler). This is a first-year kicker. No pressure. All the extra points, field goal. Those are difference makers in the game."

It was a fast start for the Merritt Island Christian scoring two plays into the game, but the team went on and fell behind 22-10. They took the lead only for Bradenton Christian to regain the lead on a pick six.

Martinson rebounded from the turnover and guided the Cougars to the comeback win throwing for 214 yards and two touchdowns and rushing for 58 yards and two touchdowns.

"It was a dog fight. It was a back-and-forth battle," Martinson said. "The quarterback was picking us apart, but we were picking them apart in the pass and the run. It was just a fight to the end."

After falling behind 22-10, Martinson threw two touchdowns to senior John Hey for a total of 123 yards. On a 4th-and-inches at the 2-yard line, Martinson reached the end zone on a QB sneak to give the Cougars a 44-34 lead with 4:18 remaining in regulation.

"We just have no quit in this team. No one had their head down. Our coaches, all of our players were just telling us to keep our heads up and we just kept on fighting," Martinson said. "Even after some interceptions and turnovers, we just kept on fighting. Even if we got hurt, the backups still did their job."

Kugler led the rushing attack with 18 carries and one reception for 204 total yards and three touchdowns. The junior scored the final Cougars touchdown on a 20-yard run following a successful stop on a Bradenton Christian onside kick attempt.

"(Kugler's) amazing. He doesn't stop," Martinson said. "He gets hurt and he comes back a couple plays later and he just keeps on fighting. He's played through sickness. He's hurt. It's amazing."

The Cougars played their first down-to-the-wire game of the season after winning their first 11 games by an average margin of 28 points. Babin said this experience couldn't have come at a better time.

"I talked to the boys at the end of the season and I said I wished we would have had a close game," Babin said. "You guys need to know what it is and you need to experience that. It's coming right now and to pull it out with the win, couldn't have asked for a better scenario than this."

Merritt Island Christian extended its state semifinal appearance streak to four years in a row. The Cougars are seeking to win their first state championship since 2023.

"It's something that our coaches didn't think we had at the start of the season, but we've gone on they had more confidence in us and they saw how the new people started to just have that dog in them," Martinson said.

The Cougars will host the No. 4 seed Sports Leadership & Management Academy on Nov. 13. SLAM defeated the No. 5 seed First Academy (Leesburg) 39-21 in the state quarterfinals.

"We've got to stay focused, stay locked in. I'm extremely hard on these guys and that is so we can achieve our ultimate goal of winning a state championship. They understand. We had a little discussion that it's going to be a tough week of practice," Babin said. "Some guys may have to start playing both ways. We may not have the luxury of a true offense and a true defense. Whatever we need to do win the game next week is what we're going to do and then if we're blessed enough to win, we'll carry that on into the state championship game."

For the second year in a row, Satellite loses in the state quarterfinals, putting an end to one of its best seasons in school history. The Scorpions finish the year 10-1 and they graduate 20 seniors.

SSAA Atlantic consolation state quarterfinals

The Bears fall at home to finish the season 6-6 and they graduate 13 seniors. It's the most wins Bayside has posted in a single season since 2014.

articles.title: Silas Demary Jr is ‘having a lot of fun’ with UConn Huskies after win over Michigan
articles.summary: Silas Demary Jr. is enjoying life with UConn after putting up a strong performance in the No. 4 Huskies’ 85-77 win over the No. 16 Michigan Wolverines on Fri...
articles.body:
Silas Demary Jr. is enjoying life with UConn after putting up a strong performance in the No. 4 Huskies' 85-77 win over the No. 16 Michigan Wolverines on Friday night.

Demary has been playing college basketball since 2023, going through his second season with the Huskies. This marks his senior campaign, making it his last chance to shine on the national stage and grow his stock for the NBA level.

Demary certainly came through with a big night against the reigning champions Michigan, who UConn lost to in the national championship game. In 36 minutes of action, he delivered a stat line of 21 points, seven rebounds, four assists, and two steals. He shot 7-of-17 from the field, including 2-of-4 from beyond the arc, and 5-of-7 from the free-throw line.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Demary reflected on the win after the game on the TNT broadcast. Having his teammates surround him in celebration, the standout player made a clear declaration on his enjoyment being part of the winning program.

"I'm having a lot of fun… more fun to come soon," Demary said.

How Silas Demary Jr., UConn played against Michigan

Silas Demary Jr. looks forward to having his senior campaign be as great as it can be. Leading UConn to serious contention for the national championship would be a great feat for the senior star.

Beating Michigan was a great step in the right direction for No. 4 UConn. They set the tone in the first half, outmatching the Wolverines 43-30 once halftime came around.

Three players scored in double-digits for UConn in the win, including Demary. Braylon Mullins led the team with 23 points, four rebounds and one steal. He shot 5-of-12 overall, including 3-of-8 from downtown, and 11-of-12 from the charity stripe. Colben Landrew came next with 14 points and eight rebounds, while Jayden Ross provided nine points and four rebounds.

The No. 4 Huskies will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Wagner Seahawks as tip-off commences on Nov. 9 at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Buatsi v Hutchinson 2 - world light-heavyweight title fight predictions
articles.summary: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Saturday's light-heavyweight world title fight between Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson.
articles.body:
Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson renew their rivalry for the vacant WBC world light-heavyweight title in Manchester on Saturday.

The British rivals first met in a highly entertaining, hard-fought contest on the undercard of Daniel Dubois' win over Anthony Joshua in September 2024.

Londoner Buatsi, 33, twice knocked down Hutchinson before going on to win by split decision.

Scotland's Hutchinson, 28, suffered the second defeat of his professional career that night but two wins since have put him in a position to fight for a first world title.

Can Buatsi repeat his victory? Or will Hutchinson gain revenge in Manchester?

BBC Sport spoke to figures from across the boxing world to get their predictions.

Chantelle Cameron - two-weight world champion

"Buatsi may stop him this time in the later rounds. I think he gets it done between rounds nine and 12."

"Willy has improved massively since the first fight, whereas I'm not sure I could say the same for Joshua."

"It's a really good fight. I think the first fight was very good - Willy was dropped a couple of times in the fight and that cost him. Otherwise, his performance was OK. He's matured a lot since that fight and is in good form.

"Buatsi has maybe just started to look old but the fact the world title is on the line... When he turned professional, everyone thought he was a shoo-in to become world champion and he hasn't achieved it yet. This is the chance, so we may see a level of Buatsi that we haven't seen in a while.

"I think it'll be really competitive but I'm just edging Hutchinson to win on points with the run of form he's on."

Viddal Riley - European cruiserweight champion

"Willy Hutchinson will get the win - it's his time. Buatsi is a tough fighter and it won't be easy but when I look at who is fresh and who has the bit between their teeth a little more - I'm backing Hutchinson."

Denzel Bentley - former WBO middleweight champion

"I'm going for a repeat for Buatsi and he finally gets his hands on a world title. It has been 10 years since he was at the Olympics and it felt like he slipped away from that batch of fighters.

"Buatsi does things in his own time and he's finally got his shot. It comes at a great time for him, it could go two ways - he's either overconfident because he's beaten Willy or his confidence could be a good thing and he could step on it early and I think it's the second one.

"I can't see Willy getting stopped - he's tough - so I'm going Buatsi on points, but he might get a knockdown."

Tony Bellew - former cruiserweight world champion

"It's very rare people can turn the rematch around when they lose the first one. On that basis, I am going for Joshua Buatsi, possibly even by late stoppage."

Zelfa Barrett - former European super-featherweight champion

"I'm going with Buatsi to win again. Hutchinson showed he was weak to the body and that could be his kryptonite.

"Hutchinson is a good fighter; he's slick and sharp, but I think Buatsi has his number and wins on points."

"Willy Hutchinson is in his physical and mental prime and I think he wins the fight. I've known Willy since he turned professional as an 18-year-old.

"He's always had the tools to be a world champion and I believe timing is everything in boxing. I believe he's also catching Buatsi at the right time."

Darren Barker - former middleweight world champion

"What a rematch. He showed his worth, his bottle and his ability did Willy Hutchinson in that first fight and proved a lot as a fighter.

"Joshua Buatsi had a very good fight with Callum Smith, although he came out second best. Not so impressive in his win over Zach Parker, it was a close fight so a lot of questions surround him and what's left.

"Hutchinson is a man in form and looks like a man who is matured both physically and mentally. This is a fantastic rematch with the WBC light-heavyweight title on the line. It promises to be an action-packed contest and the pot of gold is massive."

"A rematch that I didn't think would come around but it all makes sense with the added incentive of gold. Someone will leave as world champion. The first time they fought, it was 80-20 Buatsi for me, but Hutchinson was a lot better than I expected.

"He has now closed that gap drastically and now it's 55-45 Buatsi. How much has Callum Smith taken out of Buatsi? On the flip side, Hutchinson, after that defeat, has gone from strength to strength.

"He showed everything in his last fight against Ezra Taylor. I favour Buatsi just, but we'll see how much that Smith fight took out of him. I think Buatsi will be world champion, but I wouldn't be surprised if Willy Hutchinson walks home with gold."

articles.title: Girona-Almeria: direct duel to get closer to the top part
articles.summary: The Girona team returns to Montilivi to face a challenging match against UD Almeria, the second-placed team. After twelve rounds, the Andalusians have accumu...
articles.body:
The Girona team returns to Montilivi to face a challenging match against UD Almeria, the second-placed team. After twelve rounds, the Andalusians have accumulated 26 points, while Girona has 21, a five-point difference that gives the match special significance in the fight to move closer to the top positions.

Girona comes into the match after suffering a 1-0 defeat at the Real Sociedad B stadium. However, prior to that, they had achieved two convincing home victories: 2-0 against FC Andorra and 5-1 against Celta Fortuna. In the previous rounds, they also drew with Tenerife (1-1) and Mallorca (0-0). Their overall record stands at six wins, three draws, and three losses, with 22 goals scored and 11 conceded.

Almeria arrives at Montilivi with a solid trajectory: eight wins, two draws, and two losses in the first twelve rounds, with 23 goals scored and 10 conceded. In their last five matches, they have achieved three wins and two draws. Their most recent result was a 1-1 draw at Eibar's stadium.

The Andalusian team boasts an offensive duo that has gained prominence in recent weeks. Miguel de la Fuente and Sergio Arribas have scored seven goals between them in the last five rounds. De la Fuente provides a strong presence in the area and finishing ability, while Arribas contributes creativity and attacking runs from midfield. Attention will also be needed for Brian Cipenga, who has scored three goals this season, and Thalys, who has netted two. Their contributions expand Almeria's offensive options and require Girona to stay focused against the various threats posed by their opponent.

articles.title: Doncic’s 53 points lift Lakers as Cavs top Sixers in LeBron James’s return
articles.summary: LA Lakers star Doncic closed the first half with an astonishing shot from well beyond the half-court line.
articles.body:
Luka Doncic poured in 53 points to propel the Los Angeles Lakers to a 124-118 NBA Cup group-stage victory over Portland on Friday as LeBron James’s latest return to Cleveland ended in defeat.

Doncic’s latest big game helped the Lakers shake off a sluggish start that saw them trailing by as many as 16 points in the second quarter.

Doncic closed the first half with an astonishing shot from well beyond the half-court line, pulling the Lakers within seven points and setting the tone for their second-half surge.

The Trail Blazers had pulled within four points in the final minute when he hit a floater, and the Lakers held on for their fourth straight win.

Doncic has scored at least 40 points in six of his last seven games and joined Elgin Baylor, Kobe Bryant and George Mikan as the only Lakers players to score 40 or more in four straight regular-season contests.

“I’m having a lot of fun,” said Doncic, who added five rebounds and five assists.

“Obviously playing basketball, it’s a lot of fun for me. It’s more [fun] when you play like this and when you win games.”

The 11th 50-point game of Doncic’s career was his fourth with the Lakers – passing LeBron James and tying Mikan for the fourth most for the franchise.

James, who left the Lakers for the Philadelphia 76ers in June, made his first trip as a Sixer to Cleveland, where the Cavs spoiled his latest homecoming with a 119-95 victory that snapped Philadelphia’s five-game winning streak.

James, expected by many to opt for a third stint in Cleveland before he chose Philadelphia, was greeted by warm cheers – and scattered boos – when he was introduced.

The four-time NBA champion, playing his 24th NBA season at the age of 41, was cheered again when he exited the game late in the fourth quarter.

LeBron: ‘I did not feel in good rhythm offensively’

In between, it was a rough night for James and his teammates.

The league’s all-time leading scorer finished with eight points on three-of-12 shooting with seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and six turnovers.

Star centre Joel Embiid missed all nine of his shots from the floor, making six free throws for six points.

Jaylen Brown, like James an off-season import, led the Sixers with 20 points, but the Cavaliers seized control early and repelled every Philadelphia surge.

Donovan Mitchell scored 10 of his 23 points in the first quarter. Evan Mobley added 22 points, and Cleveland out-rebounded Philadelphia 56-42 despite the injury absence of centre Jarrett Allen.

“I did not feel in a good rhythm offensively,” James said.

“We didn’t look like much offensively. We had a couple of spurts. We were able to cut [the deficit] to three in the third quarter. But too many turnovers on my behalf.”

Friday’s games were part of NBA Cup group-stage action, which will continue throughout November.

Quarterfinals of the in-season tournament will be played December 4-5 and semifinals December 8-9 before the final on December 11.

The Boston Celtics drained a whopping 24 three-pointers on 44 attempts in a 119-80 blowout of the Hornets in Charlotte.

Jayson Tatum drilled five three-pointers on the way to a game-high 34 points for Boston, who led by as many as 46 in the wire-to-wire win.

San Antonio star Victor Wembanyama, coming off a stunning 52-point, 24-rebound performance in a win over Dallas, scored 30 points and pulled down 14 rebounds to lead the Spurs to a 124-109 victory over the Kings in Sacramento.

The Oklahoma City Thunder continued their dominance of the Grizzlies with a 128-97 win in Memphis.

Ajay Mitchell scored a career-high 35 points, and two-time defending NBA Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander added 28 for the Thunder, who notched a 13th straight regular-season win over the Grizzlies despite missing injured starters Jaylen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren.

The absences were irrelevant as the Thunder jumped to a 71-49 halftime lead.

articles.title: Franco Colapinto Drives the Alpine-Themed Renault 6 Fans Took From Argentina to Brazil
articles.summary: Franco Colapinto has just shared a special moment with a group of fans who traveled from Argentina to Brazil to support him. The fans had…
articles.body:
Franco Colapinto has just shared a special moment with a group of fans who traveled from Argentina to Brazil to support him. The fans had restored a 1977 Renault 6 and decorated it with Alpine's signature blue, pink and white colors, along with Colapinto's racing number 43. Their remarkable journey from Esperanza, Santa Fe, to Brazil covered more than 2,000 kilometers.

The three fans, Hernán Bonvín, Claudio Goddio and Pablo Quaino, had set out on the adventure with the dream of meeting their Formula 1 hero. After spotting the uniquely decorated car, Colapinto greeted the group with a smile and took a closer look at their creation.

What followed was an unforgettable surprise as the Alpine driver climbed behind the wheel and took the Renault 6 for a drive through the streets of São Paulo.

Videos of the encounter quickly spread across social media, capturing Colapinto enjoying the experience while the excited fans cheered from inside the vehicle.

The Argentine even joked about the car's radio system, asking whether it worked as he drove, prompting laughter from his passengers. The light-hearted interaction offered a memorable glimpse of the connection between the young driver and his supporters.

Seeing Colapinto drive the car they had worked months on to get going made it all worth their while. The car, which they named 'Renoleta ', became an eye-catching wonder wherever it went. It became an even more significant deal for the Argentine driver during the Brazilian GP weekend, as it highlighted the enthusiasm of South American F1 supporters.

Franco Colapinto Has Reignited Argentina's F1 Passion

Colapinto has rapidly become one of the most well-known young faces in Argentine motorsport, and his arrival in F1 has certainly rekindled the passion for the sport in Argentina. A country with a very strong motorsport tradition, his presence on the grid has been a real boost. His performances, as well as his personability, have really helped him to connect with fans of all ages.

The 23-year-old's rising profile is also a reflection of the renewed interest in F1 amongst the Argentine fans, who have taken him as an ambassador for their country in the world of motorsport.

It's not just on the track that he's been embraced, with a huge amount of social media interaction and genuine passion for him at the race meetings. He's brought the country a lot of international attention.

As he continues to build his career in F1, Colapinto has become a figure of interest for the Argentinian fanbase who are keen to see one of their own make his mark at the top of the sport. His relationship with the fans has become a key part of his public persona, and that in itself is a huge part of the appeal. It's a journey that the next generation of Argentinian F1 fans will follow closely.

Franco Colapinto Fans Can Be a Bit Too Emotional

It is hardly a secret that South American fans take sports very seriously, and things can sometimes escalate to extremities in terms of fandom. While F1 does not have a plethora of examples in this context, one of the most prominent ones came in September, when Colapinto was a primary subject of a multi-car crash in Azerbaijan.

Colapinto lost control of his car in Baku and caused a multi-car pile-up during a safety car restart, taking Lando Norris and Pierre Gasly out of the race.

Without viewing the footage and without naming anyone, Norris suggested that whoever caused the collision should be handed a one-race ban. Taking the comment to heart, Colapinto's fans flooded Norris on social media with a flurry of hate and abuse.

Gasly and a few others also got caught in the crossfire, with Colapinto labeling the behavior as something that was "not nice to see." Alpine subsequently issued a statement in which it condemned the online abuse without pointing to any particular fanbase.

The French outfit felt it was necessary for them to speak up in a difficult time, particularly given that members of the entire F1 community were being targeted.

Ultimately, the team did not want to point fingers at anyone and labeled the crash a racing incident that should be let go by the fans.

articles.title: Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur honors the late Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday with epic t-shirt
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur made a heartfelt gesture Friday, honoring franchise legend Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday. L...
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur made a heartfelt gesture Friday, honoring franchise legend Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday. LaFleur, who recently made a major quarterback change involving Gardner Minshew, arrived at his media availability wearing a shirt featuring the late safety.

The maroon shirt featured an image of Tillman wearing his No. 40 Cardinals jersey, offering a simple but meaningful tribute photo to one of the organization's most respected figures.

Cardinals reporter Mark Dalton shared a photo of LaFleur's tribute, highlighting the coach's decision to commemorate Tillman's milestone birthday.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Tillman, born November 6, 1976, played college football at Arizona State before joining the Cardinals in 1998. He spent four seasons with Arizona, establishing himself as a hard-hitting safety and earning widespread admiration for his dedication.

Following the September 11 attacks, Tillman made the extraordinary decision to leave professional football and enlist in the United States Army alongside his brother Kevin.

He served as an Army Ranger before passing away in Afghanistan on April 22, 2004, at just 27 years old.

His legacy remains deeply connected to the Cardinals, who retired his No. 40 jersey and erected a statue outside State Farm Stadium in his honor.

The tribute came as LaFleur prepared Arizona for its upcoming matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, with the Cardinals navigating significant roster changes after Jacoby Brissett's departure to the Baltimore Ravens.

Despite the demands of preparing for another divisional contest, LaFleur took time to recognize a figure whose influence extends well beyond football.

His shirt served as another reminder that Tillman's sacrifice and legacy continue to resonate throughout the Cardinals organization.

articles.title: Devils stay top with overtime victory against Stars
articles.summary: Cardiff Devils remain top of Elite League after a hard-earned 2-1 overtime victory against Dundee Stars at Vindico Arena on Friday, 6 November.
articles.body:
Cardiff Devils remain top of Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) after a hard-earned 2-1 overtime victory against Dundee Stars at Vindico Arena on Friday, 6 November.

Visiting netminder Vladislav Pestov finished with 53 saves for the Stars who frustrated a dominant home side with a resolute defensive display.

Dundee opened the scoring in the first period through Matthew DeBoer, after a breakaway from a Devils error.

The home side finally found a way through with a Brandon Estes shot from point to equalise midway through the second.

Neither side could force a regulation winner, and there were just 40 seconds left on the clock in overtime when Kristoff Kontos scored his first league goal of the season to claim the extra point for Cardiff.

"It's two points, it's a win," said a relieved Devils head coach Paul Thompson.

"We didn't make the most of the [offensive] zone time that we had from a scoring perspective, but I'm happy that Kontos made that big play to score us the OT winner."

Cardiff - who have 13 points, the same as second placed Sheffield Steelers - travel to Fife Flyers on Sunday, 8 November (17:00 GMT).
